artifacts.summary: 3-phase sequential plan (1.5h): red-then-green regression fixture, has()->type-test mutation-filter swap plus comment rewrite in validate-state.sh, full verification of the three file_scope dedup invariants.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's validate-state.sh, a failed --fix write is EXIT-CODE-INVISIBLE: the failure branch uses a raw `echo -e "${RED}[FAIL]${NC} ..."` rather than log_fail(), so it never increments FAILED, and base (non---strict) mode gates the exit code on FAILED alone while Checks 8-11 are WARN-only. Consequence for any test or caller: `--fix` exiting 0 does NOT prove a repair landed; only asserting the post-state (e.g. the duplicate is actually gone) does. Generalizes to a paired-filter hazard: when a validator runs a null-guarded REPORT filter (`($t.f // []) as $fs`) alongside a separate MUTATION filter handed to state-write.sh, the two must agree on their guard. A `has("key")` presence test is true for a literal-null value, so `has("f") then .f |= (reduce .[] ...)` aborts jq on null; the correct gate is the type test `(.f|type) == "array"`, which also preserves no-manufacture for free (null keeps its null, absent key stays absent) where a `// []` default at the assignment site would wrongly write `f: []`.
